reason: The React chat target is not built. Its reading rules (replies stay visible, the process folds, hidden rows, the retry receipt, one row per tool call, the inherited-history divider) become one pure host plan that area C4's renderer places nodes by; the turn rail, usage row and statistics are server-rendered fragments from host projections; scroll following is the first-party script's job and older history loads under browser scroll anchoring. Folding on the next message, the exchange rule and the fold animation are dropped by decision.

The trigger pipeline is kept: a slash or an at-sign at a word start opens a grouped menu that the keyboard drives without leaving the composer, Escape changes nothing and a dismissed menu stays closed. Detection, highlight and keys live in the composer island; the candidates and the menu's HTML come from host completion sources registered with complete.Registry, which may be scoped to one session.

The client-side command directory cache and the three client command kinds are not built. The menu lists area A17's command catalogue and area A14's skills through one host completion source, matched by name or translated title; a command with arguments becomes a leading chip, a picker or form is a host fragment opened from the menu, and the plus button opens the same menu without script. A command line is still never sent to the model.

File, folder and session mentions are kept with upstream's rule that the canonical text is the reference's identity. Candidates come from area A14's file and session reference services under the caller's principal, files first; a pick is an atomic chip in the island; the host parses and validates the text at admission and records the confirmed spans, from which the sent-text view draws chips.

The React rail, drop overlay, gallery factory and lightbox are replaced: a staged upload becomes an attachment chip inside the composer's text, as the owner decided in DH-ADR-21, with its progress, failure, retry and remove inside the chip; one gallery partial called from four views, and a native modal dialog with fit and actual-size views and a download link. Picking, drop, paste and progress are area C1's upload control placed in the composer form.

The transfer service that keeps an original File alive behind an application-local token is not needed: a draggable image carries a reference to its host object, a drop on a composer stages it by reference with no bytes re-uploaded, and a failure is shown in the host-rendered notice region. A few lines of first-party script set the drag data. Native desktop drag-out is dropped with the desktop application.

Download becomes a link to the host's byte routes with a download disposition, and copying an image writes a PNG the host produced to the clipboard, so no browser-side decoding or MIME normalisation is needed. Save as, the Chromium download adapter and reveal-in-folder exist only in upstream's desktop application and are dropped on record.

The behaviour is kept: one provider-grouped, searchable list behind both the composer control and the /model command, selection by route, model and effort ids, applied at the next request, and a saved selection missing from the catalogue does not block sending. It is one server-rendered picker fragment over area A04's resolved model set, redrawn in every tab when the selection or the catalogue changes.

The rating pair and the dialog become a rating partial and a form fragment over area A17's feedback service. Recording a rating sends nothing; the form then offers keep local, export, or send after a preview of exactly what would be sent. Upstream's rule that the conversation log travels with every feedback event is dropped under the owner's opt-in decision. A rating is a log event, so every tab draws it.

Masking moves from one React text renderer to the host: a pure Go package recognises upstream's published credential formats and the values the host's secret store released, every host view prints user-written text through it, and the fragment holds only the masked text. The original leaves the host only through an owner-only reveal or copy request. The log and the model request keep what the user sent.
The viewer is a host-rendered modal dialog that offers a fit view and an actual-size view that scrolls, plus a download link to the stored original, so zoom and download both exist.

The viewer is a native dialog element opened modally by the first-party script, and a modal dialog makes the rest of the page inert, so Tab cannot reach the page behind it; a real-browser scenario asserts that focus cannot leave the dialog.

The cause is a persistent script-held anchor that keeps restoring the scroll position during a touch gesture. The Go UI holds no anchor: an older page is one fragment inserted above the viewport and the browser's own scroll anchoring keeps the reading line, so nothing constrains a gesture afterwards.

The running indicator is a vector shape animated by a style sheet rule from the design system, not a 28 by 28 raster animation, so it stays sharp at any font size or pixel ratio and its animation restarts with the element.

Tool additions and removals no longer share the generic context presentation of a developer message: the reading plan gives a tool change its own row kind, and the row lists what was added and removed in full.

There are no local echoes whose order is a prediction. A message is shown only after the host admitted it, and waiting messages are drawn from the host's inbox projection in queue order, the same in every tab.

Paging by window is kept on purpose, but the fallback this bullet describes cannot occur: the turn rail is always rendered by the host from area A06's turn outline, which covers every started turn whether or not its page is loaded, and a jump requests a window around the target turn.

A preview card is a fragment the host builds from the turn outline, so a loaded and an unloaded turn give the same card and an open turn shows its latest committed assistant text. The card stays small by design; that is not a limit of data.

A command's result is not a client notice that needs a live composer to land in: area A17 logs command/run and command/done, and the result is drawn from the log by the stream in every tab, also after the session view was closed and reopened.
Save as is not offered, and copying an image still needs the browser's clipboard permission. Removed: the copy no longer depends on the browser decoding the image, because the host serves a PNG.
justification: A web page cannot choose where a download is saved or grant itself clipboard access; both belong to the browser and the user. The desktop application that offered Save as is removed by owner decision DH-ADR-18. The Download action always works and the browser's own setting can ask for a location.

reason: The start-up deadline for native downloads and the credential-free clipboard reader describe the Electron download adapter of upstream's desktop application. The Go design has no desktop application, so neither mechanism exists; a download is an ordinary response the browser handles.
After a browser download the page still cannot offer to reveal the saved file, because it is never told where the file went.
justification: No browser reports a download's destination to the page that started it; the browser's own downloads list offers the reveal action. For a file that already exists in the workspace the host path is known and its open-in-folder action belongs to the area that owns opening host files.

reason: Dragging a file out of the page into another application still depends on the browser implementing the DownloadURL drag type, which only Chromium-family browsers do. Removed: there are no application-local tokens, a drag names a host object that any tab or window of the same browser can use, and remote images are served from the host's origin so the unreadable cross-origin case does not arise.
justification: The web platform has no cross-browser way to hand an original file to another application during a drag, and the native path existed only in the desktop application removed by DH-ADR-18. The Download action is the route that works everywhere, and the scenario records the browsers where drag-out is unsupported.

reason: The cause is a Blob URL owned by the page that is revoked when the transfer ends. The drag now names a durable host URL that stays valid for as long as the object is stored, so a receiver that reads late finds it. Delivery to another application is asserted in a real-browser scenario or recorded as unsupported for that browser.

Session-scope registration exists: a completion source registered through one agent's scope context is listed only for that session and is removed with the agent, which is the ordinary cordis scope rule; a local test asserts both.

The split between where a slot's type merge lives and who owns the slot exists because of the import direction between two TypeScript packages and the client slot map. The Go design has no client slots; the menu is a fragment that the composer's own component renders.

The form is rendered by the host with area A17's limits as field attributes, for a message note and for a session remark alike, and an oversized value is answered with a 422 that marks the field and keeps the form open, so the user learns the limit while writing and a remark is bounded.
A rating is a committed log event, and the event stream's fragment for that event redraws the message's rating control out of band in every tab that shows the session, without a reconnect.

The rating control is a partial keyed by message id, not a part of the chat view. The conversation places it in each turn's footer, and the trajectory page (ui-work.md DH-D-UIWORK-1) places it on every assistant-message record; each bar of the timing overview links to its record. DH-T-UIWORK-1 checks the control on the trajectory record.

A model can be chosen before the first message: the picker works on a blank session, and session creation accepts an initial selection, which the agent contract already carries in its create options. Subagent sessions deliberately get no picker of their own; that is a rule of the delegation area, not a missing feature here.

Selection by ids is kept as correct. The unselectable failure row that lasts until reload is removed: area A04 serves the last good listing and then the embedded catalogue, the picker fragment reloads when the model set changes, and a failed provider is a row with a retry that requests the fragment again.

The picker still offers only advertised effort levels, because a free value would fail at the provider. The cause of a missing Effort row is removed: effort levels are catalogue data that an operator can correct per model in the route's overlay, so a model whose adapter reports nothing can still be given its levels.
The composer control and the /model command open the same picker view, so a badge appears on every row in both, and the control's accessible name is rendered by the host with the badge text in it.

A completion source that errs or times out is shown as a named group that could not load, with a retry, and the other groups are still listed. A session mention the caller may not read is refused at admission with the chip marked and the draft kept, so that failure no longer arrives after acceptance and ends a turn.

The bullet describes a client plugin that cannot work when its host provider is not mounted, because upstream's client is a separate program. In the Go design every candidate comes from the host by construction and the browser has no file access; a composition without the file source simply has no file group.

A sent mention still does not follow a later rename or deletion of its file. Removed: the answer no longer depends on the page load, because the host checks the path once at admission and records the result with the message, so every tab and every reload draws the same thing.
justification: The event stream requires a fragment to be a function of the session log alone, so that a replay draws what the live stream drew; a chip that tracked the filesystem would break that. The chip opens the file preview, which shows a missing file as missing.

reason: The session completion source asks area A14's session reference service, which finds sessions by body text through the session search index and not only by id, directory and title.
A credential in no published format is still drawn as written, and named assignments stay plain. Narrowed: any value the host's own secret store has released is masked whatever its shape.
justification: Masking by name, such as every value after password=, would hide ordinary values that use the same names and would train users to ignore the masks. Recognition by published format keeps false positives near zero; the store-released values cover the credentials the harness itself knows.

reason: The cause is that masking is attached to one renderer. Masking is now a pure host function that every view printing user-written text calls: bubbles, queued rows, rail previews, titles and excerpts. The editable draft is deliberately shown as typed, and the host warns before sending when the draft appears to contain a credential.
The sent-text view passes a mention's label through the same masking function before it draws the chip, so a credential inside a file mention is masked in the chip; a local test asserts it.

Final verdict after reading the note: keep. One row per call id passes through preparing, start and result, and the preparing stage changes no event and no dispatch timing. In the Go design the reading plan gives the three stages one row, the preparing stage is drawn from the live frame and the other two from durable events, and area C4 draws the card.

Final verdict: replace the mechanism, keep the reuse. Four image slots filled by one gallery factory become one gallery partial called by the views of user messages, assistant output, tool results and trajectory rows. Replacement of the gallery by a client plugin is not offered, because there is no client plugin runtime.

Final verdict: replace. The note separates where the reasoning body goes from the default way to draw it, so that a wrapper such as translation can reuse the default. On the host the same split is a declared region plus a shared partial; the slot priorities and factory registration are React mechanics. The reasoning node itself belongs to area C4.

Final verdict: replace. The exchange rule exists so that a turn started by a notice does not fold the previous turn when folding waits for the next message. The Go design folds a process group once, at its own turn's end, so no later turn can fold it and the rule has nothing left to decide; the plan keeps the row positions input, process, reply and turn-level.

Final verdict: replace. The single frame clock removes a visible jump between two script-driven fold paths. A fold in the Go UI is one replacement of a process group at a durable event, with the browser's scroll anchoring holding the reading line, so there is no script motion to coordinate; the goal of no jump is checked in a real-browser scenario.

Final verdict: replace. The precomputed batch start keeps a reserved slot stable while React re-renders local steering echoes. There are no local echoes: waiting input, steering included, is drawn by the host from the inbox projection in the host's order, so the order is known when the region is rendered.

Final verdict: replace. The note moves retained drag files out of a React ancestor into one plugin, because the original must survive its source unmounting and a failure must outlive its panel. A drag in the Go UI carries a reference to a host object, so nothing is retained in the page, and a failure is a host-rendered notice. The measured finding that a browser File does not survive a same-page drop is the reason the reference is used.

Final verdict: replace. Rendering a fenced block by its language (mathematics, diffs, later diagrams) stays a requirement, but Markdown is rendered on the host, so the dispatch by language belongs to the host renderer of area C4 and not to a keyed client slot that the chat view passes down. This area passes nothing to it.

Final verdict: keep. A folded turn hides its process and never its replies, because the last message by position is often an addendum and the real answer would fold away. The reading plan applies the rule, and the preference with the values all and final is kept as a host preference.

Final verdict: replace the scanner, keep its inputs and its gate. The hand-built matcher exists to avoid regular-expression backtracking in JavaScript; Go's regexp package guarantees time linear in the input. The table of credential formats, the rule that overlapping candidates join the earliest, and the performance gate for text with and without credentials carry over as a table test and a budget test.

Final verdict: adopt the behaviour, drop the machinery. Earlier history is fetched before the reader reaches the top and must not move what is being read. The load-earlier control requests the previous page when it scrolls into view, and the fragment is inserted above the viewport under the browser's scroll anchoring, so there is no held page, no intent state and no anchor to manage. A browser without scroll anchoring is recorded by the scenario.
